spec: AES MixColumns (forward), a 32x32 GF(2) linear map. Column matrix [[2,3,1,1],[1,2,3,1],[1,1,2,3],[3,1,1,2]] over GF(2^8) with reduction polynomial 0x11b.
note: sha256_circuit_json is over the exact circuit JSON file bytes as written. sha256_canonical_gates is SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 bytes of the compact JSON string {"inputCount":32,"gates":[...]} with keys in that order; reproduce it with scripts/reproduce_canonical_hashes.py.

circuits.outputConvention: output j (j in 0..31) is MixColumns output bit j; bit j = bit (j mod 8) of state byte (j div 8), least-significant-bit-first within each byte. It is produced at internal signal index outputSignals[j].

verified.method: checked against AES MixColumns rebuilt from GF(2^8) in verify.py, and against 32 basis-vector responses in the Verilog testbench

circuits.claim: Uses fewer 2-input XOR gates than the smallest published counts we are aware of for AES MixColumns: 91 XORs (Lin, Xiang, Zeng, and Zhang, CT-RSA 2021, s-XOR model, which translates instruction-for-gate into 2-input XOR circuits) and Maximov's explicit 92-gate circuit; we do not make an optimality claim.

circuits.claim: Uses fewer 2-input XOR gates than the 99-gate depth-3 AES MixColumns point reported by Shi, Feng, and Xu (ToSC 2023). Depth 3 is the known minimum depth for this map (an output depending on w inputs needs depth at least ceil(log2(w)), and MixColumns has outputs of weight 7); we do not make an optimality claim on the gate count.
